newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay aims to up fares in mid-December.
newsitem.headline: Cathay aims to up fares in mid-December.

text.p: Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Thursday it aims to raise air ticket prices by three percent in mid-December following approval by the Civil Aviation Department (CAD) for such a move.
A Cathay spokesperson said the CAD had given its approval on Wednesday.
Cathay said the International Air Transport Association (IATA) had proposed that airlines increase their fares by three percent by December 15 to offset higher fuel prices.
"We are aiming for the middle of December in accordance with the IATA but if negotiations (with counterparts on each route) take longer it might be delayed," the Cathay spokesperson said.
She said the airline would calculate what the three percent increase represented on each route and give the figures to the CAD and the designated carriers on each route.
"Because our agreements are bilateral we need the approval of the designated carriers of each route," she added.

Kwan Chuk-fai, manager of corporate communications, said last week that the three percent rise on published fares could only partly compensate for an increase of at least 30 percent in fuel costs seen over the past 12 months.
Fuel cost account for about 15 percent of Cathay's operating costs, he added.
